title: Platform Target
description: Which platform(s) are you designing for? This scopes the downstream decisions and previews.
cpNote: Scope first: the platform constrains nav idioms, density, and which preview columns are relevant (Hick — prune the space before deciding details).

options.label: Web
options.desc: Desktop + responsive web app. Pointer-first, generous canvas, left-nav or top-nav idioms. e.g. Linear, Vercel, Notion web.

options.label: Mobile (iOS)
options.desc: iPhone-first native. Tab bar, sheets, 44px touch targets, SF Symbols. e.g. Things, Robinhood, Instagram.

options.label: macOS
options.desc: Mac desktop app. Toolbar + sidebar, compact controls, menu bar, windowed. e.g. Things for Mac, Linear desktop.

options.label: Multiple
options.desc: Design a shared system across web + iOS + macOS. Previews show all platforms; tokens carry per-platform layers.

title: Primary Navigation Structure
description: What is the top-level navigation / layout skeleton? This cascade-constrains every screen.
cpNote: Nav structure is the skeleton every screen hangs on; choose it before color/type/density (general→specific cascade).

options.label: Left Sidebar Nav
options.desc: Persistent left rail of destinations. Dense apps, many top-level areas. e.g. Linear, Slack, Notion.

options.label: Top Nav Bar
options.desc: Horizontal top bar of primary links. Fewer destinations, content-forward. e.g. Vercel, Stripe docs.

options.label: Bottom Tab Bar
options.desc: 3–5 bottom tabs, thumb-reachable. Mobile-native primary nav. e.g. Instagram, Robinhood.

options.label: None / Single Surface
options.desc: No persistent chrome — one focused surface or a flow. Onboarding, single-purpose tools, kiosks.

title: Tab Bar Style
description: How should the primary navigation tabs look and behave?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 says: Nav states use text + bottom border (never background boxes). But real apps break this rule in nuanced ways.

options.label: Icon + Label (Classic)
options.desc: SF Symbols icon above a 10pt label. Active state uses tint color fill + colored label. Used by: Spotify, Robinhood, Instagram.

options.label: Icon Only (Minimal)
options.desc: No labels. Active icon gets filled or colored pill background. Saves vertical space, relies on icon clarity. Used by: Linear, Things 3.

options.label: Floating Pill Bar
options.desc: Tab bar floats above the safe area, detached from screen edge. Rounded pill shape, glass-morphism or solid. Used by: some fintech apps.

options.label: Auto-Hiding on Scroll
options.desc: Tab bar slides down and hides when user scrolls content, reappears on scroll-up. More content area. Used by: Medium, YouTube.

title: Active Tab Indicator
description: How should the selected/active tab be indicated?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 specifies text + 2px bottom border for selected nav state. But iOS apps use a variety of patterns.

options.label: Color Fill + Label Color
options.desc: Active icon switches to filled variant + label turns accent color. Clean, systematic, what iOS expects natively.

options.label: Pill Background
options.desc: Active tab gets a rounded pill/capsule background behind the icon. Creates a contained, button-like active state.

options.label: Dot Indicator
options.desc: Small dot below active icon. Minimal visual weight. Icon stays outlined. Used by apps that prefer restraint.

options.label: Top Border Line
options.desc: Thin 2–3px line appears above the active tab icon (at top of tab bar). Architectural feel, references desktop tab conventions.

title: Back Navigation Pattern
description: How should users navigate back through hierarchy?
cpNote: Swipe-right-from-left-edge is Apple standard. But the visual affordance and label treatment varies significantly.

options.label: Back + Parent Title
options.desc: "← Settings" — back button shows parent screen name. Provides context on where you came from. HIG default.

options.label: Chevron Only
options.desc: Just the ← chevron, no label text. Clean. Loses contextual information. Used by apps with deep hierarchy or limited header space.

options.label: X Close Button
options.desc: × in top-right for modal/sheet contexts, ← for pushed navigation. Distinct affordance signals modality vs hierarchy.

title: Bottom Sheet Handle
description: How is the drag handle styled on bottom sheets?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 recommends bottom sheets over modals for detail views. The handle treatment signals draggability.

options.label: Gray Pill (Standard)
options.desc: 36×5px rounded pill in gray-300 at top of sheet. Standard iOS 15+ native appearance. Universal recognition.

options.label: Dark Pill on Card
options.desc: Same pill but on a dark/colored sheet background. The pill uses a lighter opacity. Popular in media and map apps.

options.label: No Handle, Drag Title
options.desc: No visible handle. Title area serves as drag zone. Cleaner, but lower discoverability. Must be taught or assumed.

options.label: Full Top Bar with Handle
options.desc: Header row with title + close button, plus pill handle above header. Most affordance, most chrome.

title: Sheet Detent Behavior
description: How should bottom sheets size and snap?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 defines 3 sizes: 40vh small, 60vh medium, 85vh large. But detent-aware snapping has richer patterns.

options.label: Fixed Half Sheet
options.desc: Sheet opens to exactly ~50% and stays. No drag resize. Context remains visible behind. Best for simple overlays.

options.label: Two-Stop Snap
options.desc: Sheet snaps between compact (~30%) and expanded (~85%). Drag crosses midpoint to transition. Maps-style.

options.label: Continuous Drag (Free)
options.desc: Sheet can be dragged freely to any height without snapping. Gives full user control. Higher cognitive load.

title: Swipe-to-Reveal Actions
description: How should hidden actions appear on list item swipe?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: right = positive (save), left = negative (delete). 80px threshold. The visual treatment varies widely.

options.label: Icon + Label Button
options.desc: Swiping reveals rectangular colored button(s) with icon + text label. Maximum clarity. Used by Apple Mail, Reminders.

options.label: Icon-Only Action
options.desc: Actions appear as icon-only circles or squares. Saves space, requires icon recognition. Used by Telegram, Robinhood.

options.label: Full-Width Destructive
options.desc: Swiping far left triggers red to fill the full row width — full swipe = immediate delete. Power-user pattern.

title: Tap / Press Feedback
description: How should interactive elements respond to a tap press?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: active:scale-[0.98] + 100ms ease-out. But the scale amount and animation curve choices create very different feels.

options.label: Scale Press-In
options.desc: Element scales down to ~0.95–0.98 on press. Tactile feel. Clean spring return on release. Standard iOS behavior.

options.label: Opacity Dim
options.desc: Element fades to ~60% opacity on press, returns to 100% on release. No scale. Used for links and ghost buttons.

options.label: Background Highlight
options.desc: Row/cell background flashes to a gray or tinted highlight color on press. Native iOS table view behavior.

options.label: Contained Ripple
options.desc: Circular ripple expands from tap point within the element bounds. More expressive, not native iOS but used in some polished apps.

title: Primary Button Shadow & Depth
description: How should primary action buttons convey elevation and interactivity?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 emphasizes Affordance Theory — interactive elements must visually signal interactivity. Shadow is one tool.

options.label: Flat (No Shadow)
options.desc: Solid fill color, no shadow. Clean, modern, system-aligned. Color contrast carries all the affordance weight.

options.label: Soft Drop Shadow
options.desc: 4–8px soft shadow in button color (colored shadow, not gray). Creates lift effect. Popular in fintech / productivity apps.

options.label: Inner Highlight Rim
options.desc: Top edge of button has a subtle lighter stroke (1px), bottom edge darker. Simulates lighting angle. Skeuomorphic-lite.

options.label: Glass / Frosted
options.desc: Semi-transparent background with blur. Adapts to content behind. Apple uses this in control center, Siri, now Liquid Glass.

title: Screen Transition Style
description: How should screens animate when navigating between them?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: motion communicates meaning. Push transitions reinforce hierarchy. But the curve + distance matter.

options.label: Slide Push (Standard)
options.desc: New screen slides in from right, previous slides left. Depth implies hierarchy. Standard iOS push navigation.

options.label: Hero Expansion
options.desc: Tapped card element expands and morphs into the new screen. Maintains visual continuity. Used by App Store, Photos.

options.label: Cross-Fade
options.desc: Screens dissolve into each other. No directional implication. Works well for tab switches and non-hierarchical navigation.

options.label: Slide Up (Modal)
options.desc: Screen slides up from bottom. Implies a layer on top. Used for modal contexts. Swipe down to dismiss.

title: Pull-to-Refresh Animation
description: What should the pull-to-refresh indicator look and feel like?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: 60px threshold, spinner during refresh. But the visual animation carries the feel of the app.

options.label: Native iOS Spinner
options.desc: Standard UIActivityIndicator in gray. Appears when threshold reached. Disappears on complete. Feels "default app".

options.label: Progress Arc
options.desc: Arc/circle draws itself as user pulls, matching pull progress 1:1. Full circle = trigger. Tactile and satisfying.

options.label: Logo / Brand Animation
options.desc: Brand icon animates during pull. Progressive drawing or morph. High-identity but requires investment. Robinhood, Snapchat.

title: List Item Separator
description: How should items in a list be visually separated?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 core: group borders + dividers, not individual borders. But iOS has strong native divider conventions.

options.label: Inset Hairline
options.desc: Thin 0.5pt hairline divider, inset from left by icon width (~16px). Standard iOS list. Implies grouped content.

options.label: Full-Width Line
options.desc: Full-width hairline edge-to-edge. Stronger visual separation. Used when list rows are more distinct from each other.

options.label: Card Per Row
options.desc: Each list item is its own card with rounded corners and shadow/border. No hairlines. Used by many modern apps.

options.label: Whitespace Only
options.desc: No lines. Items separated by consistent vertical whitespace (12–16px). Clean, requires good typography to work.

title: Search Bar Position & Style
description: Where and how should the search bar live in a list or feed view?
cpNote: Apple HIG: search can be in nav bar row 3, visible always, or hidden until pull-down. Each changes the interaction model.

options.label: In Nav Bar (Scrolls Away)
options.desc: Search bar sits below large title, scrolls off screen with content. Users pull down to reveal. HIG default.

options.label: Sticky Top Bar
options.desc: Search is fixed at top, always visible, never scrolls away. Sacrifices 44–56px of content space permanently.

options.label: Dedicated Search Tab
options.desc: Magnifying glass as a primary tab in the tab bar. Tapping opens a full search experience. Used by Twitter/X, Pinterest.

title: Content Loading Skeleton
description: How should content areas look while data is loading?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: skeleton screens for 1–3s waits. Shimmer 1.5s. Match three-line layout. But shimmer direction varies.

options.label: Shimmer Left-to-Right
options.desc: Gray placeholder blocks with light shimmer that sweeps left-to-right. The most recognized loading pattern.

options.label: Pulse Fade
options.desc: Placeholder blocks fade in and out (opacity pulse). No directional shimmer. Calmer, but less progress-suggestive.

options.label: Blurred Content
options.desc: Actual content is shown but blurred, then sharpens when loaded. Shows real layout immediately. Used by some news apps.

title: Empty State Illustration Style
description: How should an empty state communicate "nothing here yet"?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: first-time empty = value promise + setup CTA. Encouraging tone. But the visual language varies dramatically.

options.label: System Icon + Text
options.desc: Large SF Symbol (64pt) in gray, followed by title and subtitle. Clean, fast, system-native. Used by Apple apps.

options.label: Custom Illustration
options.desc: On-brand illustration or scene image. More personality, higher visual engagement. Requires design investment.

options.label: Text Only (Ultra Minimal)
options.desc: No icon or illustration. Just a centered message and CTA button. Works well for task/productivity apps with clean aesthetic.

title: In-App Toast / Notification
description: How should brief feedback messages appear after actions?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: confirmation must state what happened + what changed. Neutral to celebratory tone by context.

options.label: Top Banner
options.desc: Full-width banner drops from top (below status bar). High visibility, used for errors and important confirmations.

options.label: Bottom Pill / Snackbar
options.desc: Compact pill floats above tab bar at bottom center. Less disruptive, no content overlap. Used by Spotify, Linear.

options.label: Inline Context Toast
options.desc: Toast appears near the element that triggered it, not at screen edges. Precise spatial feedback.

options.label: Center HUD
options.desc: Square frosted HUD appears center-screen with icon + text. Classic iOS pattern (share sheets, AirDrop success, etc.).

title: Button & Surface Gradient Style
description: How should color gradients be applied to buttons, cards, and key surfaces?
cpNote: Flat fills are the CP 6.4.1 default. But gradient depth signals premium quality and adds tactile weight to CTAs.

options.label: Linear Gradient
options.desc: Top-to-bottom or angled linear gradient on buttons/cards. Slight lightening at top, darkening at bottom. Adds depth without complexity.

options.label: Mesh / Aurora Gradient
options.desc: Multi-point mesh gradient (iOS 18 MeshGradient API). Colors blend organically like northern lights. Used for hero surfaces and splash screens.

options.label: Duotone Wash
options.desc: Two-color gradient overlaid on content or imagery. Strong brand identity. Works on cards, headers, and section backgrounds.

options.label: Flat Solid Fill
options.desc: Pure flat color. No gradient. Maximum clarity and system-native feel. Color precision over depth.

title: Dark Mode Surface Treatment
description: How should surface layers be differentiated in dark mode?
cpNote: True black vs near-black is the single biggest dark mode quality signal. Elevation must be perceptible without color.

options.label: True Black Base
options.desc: #000 background with #111-#1C1C1E surface cards. Maximum OLED battery savings. Stark, premium contrast. Twitter/X, Apollo.

options.label: Layered Near-Black
options.desc: Base #111, cards #1C1C1E, overlays #2C2C2E. Subtle elevation via brightness steps. Apple system UI native pattern.

options.label: Deep Chromatic Dark
options.desc: Dark mode with a hue tint (deep navy, deep purple, dark forest). Not pure gray — color temperature carries brand identity.

options.label: Glass / Frosted Surfaces
options.desc: Cards and surfaces use blur + transparency instead of solid fills. iOS 26 Liquid Glass direction. Content bleeds through layers.

title: Accent Color Application
description: How liberally and where should the brand/accent color be applied?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: accent only on primary CTA and critical state. Best-in-class apps develop a more nuanced, systemic accent language.

options.label: CTA-Only Restraint
options.desc: Accent appears only on the single primary CTA and key interactive states. Everything else neutral. Maximum signal strength per use.

options.label: Semantic Accent System
options.desc: Accent for CTAs, active states, progress bars, selection, highlights. Secondary accent for success/error. Linear, Notion pattern.

options.label: Expressive Accent Spread
options.desc: Accent bleeds into section backgrounds, gradients, icon fills, and headers. Brand-immersive. Spotify, Robinhood, Duolingo.

title: Display & Heading Treatment
description: How should headings be styled beyond just size — weight, tracking, case?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1 defines three-line hierarchy. But weight contrast, tracking, and case treatment separate good from great type.

options.label: SF Pro System Native
options.desc: Pure SF Pro at system-defined sizes. Large Title 34pt, Title 28pt, Headline 17pt semibold. Invisible, familiar, zero friction.

options.label: Extreme Weight Contrast
options.desc: Black/Heavy weight for display (700-900), Regular for body. The delta creates strong visual hierarchy without extreme size differences.

options.label: Tight Tracking on Headings
options.desc: Large headings use tight letter-spacing (-0.03em to -0.05em). Feels deliberately designed. Linear, Arc, Stripe signature.

options.label: Custom Brand Font
options.desc: Custom or licensed typeface for display text, SF Pro for body. Brand voice in every headline. High investment, high return.

title: Numeric & Data Display Style
description: How should numbers, stats, prices, and data values be typeset?
cpNote: Numbers carry precision expectations. Tabular alignment, mono spacing, and weight hierarchy matter more than most designers realize.

options.label: Hero Number Display
options.desc: Primary metric huge (48-64pt), thin or regular weight. Supporting label small and muted below. Apple Health, finance app pattern.

options.label: Monospaced Tabular
options.desc: Numbers use tabular-nums or monospaced font. Columns align perfectly. Decimals never shift. Robinhood, trading app standard.

options.label: Mixed-Weight Numerics
options.desc: Integer part bold/heavy, decimal part regular/light. Visual weight on significant digits. Stripe, Monzo, Revolut signature.

title: Tab Bar Icon Animation
description: How do tab bar icons animate when tapped to switch tabs?
cpNote: The tab tap is one of the most frequent interactions in any app. Its quality signals the craft level of the entire product.

options.label: Instant State Swap
options.desc: Icon switches immediately from outlined to filled on tap. No animation. Native iOS default. Fast and unobtrusive.

options.label: Spring Bounce
options.desc: Icon scales up briefly (1.2x) with a spring bounce on tap, then settles to normal. Satisfying physical feedback. Instagram, Threads.

options.label: Outline to Fill Morph
options.desc: Icon smoothly morphs from outlined to filled variant. 200ms ease-out. Intentionally designed, not a default fallback.

options.label: Lottie / Rive Animated Icon
options.desc: Fully custom animated icon using Lottie or Rive. Each tab has a unique micro-animation on select. Duolingo, Spotify-level craft.

title: Haptic Feedback Strategy
description: How should haptic feedback be used and layered across the app?
cpNote: Wrong haptics break trust faster than no haptics. Every vibration is a claim: "something meaningful just happened."

options.label: Key Moments Only
options.desc: Haptics only on: destructive confirm, success completion, and errors. Nothing else. Every haptic is meaningful and intentional.

options.label: Standard UIKit Vocabulary
options.desc: Light tick on selection changes. Medium thud on confirmations. Double-tap pattern for notifications. UIFeedbackGenerator system.

options.label: Custom CHHaptic Patterns
options.desc: Custom CHHapticEngine patterns: waveform on audio scrub, resistance on swipe threshold, multi-tap on milestone. Core Haptics API.

title: Toggle & Switch Animation
description: How should boolean toggles and segmented controls animate?
cpNote: The humble toggle is one of the most frequent controls. Its animation quality is a proxy for the app's overall craft level.

options.label: Native UISwitch
options.desc: Standard iOS UISwitch. Thumb slides with spring. Immediate recognition. No customization — leverage the platform.

options.label: Spring Stretch Thumb
options.desc: Custom toggle: thumb stretches horizontally as it slides (rubber-band), then snaps to new position. Spring 0.5s, 0.6 damping.

options.label: Segmented Pill Slider
options.desc: Pill glides between 2-4 labeled segments with spring. Used for mode switching. Linear, Notion, Apple Maps pattern.

options.label: Checkbox to Checkmark Morph
options.desc: Circle morphs into filled checkmark with a pop animation on select. Reverse on deselect. Reminders, Things, OmniFocus pattern.

title: Onboarding Flow Structure
description: How should the first-run onboarding be structured overall?
cpNote: Every extra onboarding screen costs ~10% of users. The goal: first value moment under 60 seconds.

options.label: Value-First (Show Don't Tell)
options.desc: Drop user straight into the app with a demo or pre-filled state. Explain features in context, not before. Linear, Arc pattern.

options.label: Progressive Disclosure Steps
options.desc: 3-5 screens, one key concept per screen. Progress indicator visible. Skip always available. Clear and educational without overwhelming.

options.label: Interactive Tutorial
options.desc: First session IS the onboarding. Real actions, real rewards, first win in <2 min. Dopamine before account creation.

options.label: Personalization Quiz
options.desc: 3-7 questions that customize the experience before launch. Sets goals, context, and commitment. Calm, Headspace, Noom.

title: Onboarding Progress Indicator
description: How should users know where they are in the onboarding flow?
cpNote: Progress indicators reduce drop-off by signaling the end is near. Showing 8+ dots creates anxiety instead of relief.

options.label: Dot Pagination
options.desc: Row of dots, active dot filled or enlarged. Best for 3-5 steps. Familiar from intro carousels and stories.

options.label: Linear Progress Bar
options.desc: Thin horizontal bar fills left-to-right with each step. Strong completion pull. Duolingo, fitness app standard.

options.label: Step Counter Text
options.desc: "Step 2 of 5" text label. Honest and clear. Works for longer flows (5-10 steps) where dots look cluttered.

options.label: No Indicator
options.desc: No progress shown. Each screen is self-contained. Best for very short (1-2 screen) or value-first onboarding.

title: Onboarding Animation Style
description: How should onboarding screens animate to create delight and set tone?
cpNote: Onboarding is the first and most-seen screen in your app. Animation quality here sets the bar for everything that follows.

options.label: Slide + Parallax
options.desc: Screens slide horizontally. Background moves slower than foreground (parallax layers). Creates depth without complexity.

options.label: Lottie Scene Animations
options.desc: Each screen features a unique Lottie animation — character, object, or scene. Plays on enter, loops subtly. Maximum delight.

options.label: Morphing Shape Transitions
options.desc: Central illustration morphs into next screen's illustration. Shape continuity across all steps. Magical and seamless. Arc, Pitch.

options.label: Staggered Element Entry
options.desc: Elements enter sequentially: illustration -> headline -> subtitle -> CTA. 60-80ms stagger. Feels purposefully designed.

title: Profile Header Layout
description: How should the user profile header be structured and styled?
cpNote: The profile header is identity real estate. Every pixel communicates user ownership and the app's design quality.

options.label: Cover Photo + Overlapping Avatar
options.desc: Full-width cover photo with circular avatar overlapping its bottom edge. Name + bio below. Twitter, GitHub, LinkedIn pattern.

options.label: Large Centered Avatar
options.desc: 100-120pt centered circular avatar on plain/gradient background. Name + role prominent below. Clean and focused.

options.label: Compact Card Header
options.desc: Small avatar left-aligned with name, role, and stats right-aligned. Card format, not full-bleed. Efficient for in-app settings/profile.

options.label: Dynamic Gradient Background
options.desc: Header background is an auto-generated gradient from avatar/brand colors. No photo required. Identity-driven design.

title: Avatar Style & Edit Pattern
description: How is the user avatar displayed, and how do users update it?
cpNote: Avatar editing is often a first-session action. Friction here signals app quality before a user has seen anything else.

options.label: Tap to Edit (Camera Badge)
options.desc: Small camera/pencil badge bottom-right of avatar. Tap opens photo picker with circular crop. Most recognized pattern.

options.label: Long Press Action Sheet
options.desc: Long press reveals action sheet: "Take Photo", "Choose Library", "Remove". No persistent badge — cleaner surface.

options.label: Generated Default Avatar
options.desc: No photo? Auto-generate: initials in brand color, abstract shape, or gradient pattern. Notion, GitHub Identicons, Apple Mail.

options.label: Animated Status Ring
options.desc: Animated gradient ring around avatar signals content status (new post, active, premium). Instagram Stories, BeReal pattern.

title: Profile Stats & Activity Display
description: How should user stats, streaks, and activity history be visualized?
cpNote: Stats are behavioral UI. The right visualization turns a number into a habit driver. The wrong one makes it feel like reporting.

options.label: Stat Row (Number + Label)
options.desc: Horizontal row of 2-4 stats: large number over small muted label. Followers / Posts / Following. Twitter, Instagram standard.

options.label: Activity Heatmap Grid
options.desc: GitHub-style contribution grid. Days as colored squares, density = activity. Streak highlights. Duolingo, Strava, GitHub.

options.label: Progress Rings
options.desc: Circular progress rings (Apple Activity style). Each ring = a metric. Fill animates on screen load. Goal-oriented apps.

options.label: Rich Stat Cards
options.desc: Each stat has its own card with sparkline trend, delta from last period, and context label. Finance, health, productivity apps.

title: Goal / Achievement Celebration
description: How does the app celebrate completing a task, streak, or milestone?
cpNote: CP 6.4.1: reward completion with appropriate motion. Intensity must match significance — confetti for a todo is noise.

options.label: Confetti Burst
options.desc: Confetti particles rain from top of screen. 1-2 second burst, brand-color matched. Duolingo, Robinhood milestone pattern.

options.label: Checkmark Morph + Ripple
options.desc: Circle draws into checkmark with spring animation. Ripple pulse radiates outward. Subtle but deeply satisfying. Things, Streaks.

options.label: Full-Screen Takeover
options.desc: Screen takes over with the celebration: animated trophy, mascot, or color flash. For rare major milestones only. Duolingo streak.

options.label: Score Tick + Glow
options.desc: Number ticks up with a satisfying count animation. Soft glow pulses around the element. Score +points popups. Linear, Notion.

title: App Launch / Splash Screen
description: What happens in the first 0.5-1.5 seconds when the app opens?
cpNote: The launch screen is mandatory on iOS. Its animation quality is a first impression that sets tone before a single tap.

options.label: Logo Fade In/Out
options.desc: Logo fades in on brand color background, then fades to first screen. Clean, fast, professional. Works for any brand.

options.label: Logo Draw / Assemble
options.desc: Logo draws itself (SVG stroke animation) or assembles from parts. 600-900ms. Memorable and distinctive. High craft signal.

options.label: Splash Morphs Into UI
options.desc: Launch shape expands and morphs into the first screen UI elements. No cut — continuous transformation. Pitch, Linear approach.

options.label: Ambient Particle / Mesh
options.desc: Background has ambient particle, wave, or mesh gradient animation during load. Logo static center. Premium, atmospheric.

title: Scroll Physics & Behavior
description: How should scroll behavior feel at edges, during interaction, and between sections?
cpNote: Apple scroll physics are famous for a reason. Top apps tune beyond defaults to create a signature tactile identity.

options.label: iOS System Default
options.desc: Standard UIScrollView physics. Rubber-band at edges, momentum deceleration. The baseline every user knows. Never wrong.

options.label: Sticky Section Headers
options.desc: Section headers stick to top as content scrolls beneath. Context always visible. Apple Contacts, Mail, App Store pattern.

options.label: Parallax Background
options.desc: Background image or gradient scrolls at 40-60% of content speed. Creates depth and layering. Profile headers, hero sections.

options.label: Snap-to-Card Paging
options.desc: Scroll snaps to each card. One card fills view at a time. Prevents partial views. App Store, Apple TV, Tinder pattern.
